messages.content: is i have took the book right?
use i have taken the book. with have in that sentence, use taken rather than took.
can i use took without have?
yes. i took the book yesterday is correct.
now make a question using did.
did you take the book yesterday?
why take there?
did goes with take in that question. taken goes with have, and took can tell what happened without either word.
use take, took, and taken in three short sentences.
i take the book home each day. i took it home yesterday. i have taken it home before.
only give those sentences again.
i take the book home each day. i took it home yesterday. i have taken it home before.
can you know i really took a book home from those grammar examples?
no. they are examples unless you tell me they are facts about your day.
only give the sentence with have again.
i have taken it home before.
write a longer story about a child asked to bring a book but not knowing where it needs to go. make the first request need more detail.

a child was standing near the shelf when his sister called from another room and asked him to bring the book. he took it to the kitchen, where they usually read together. she was waiting by the front door instead. when he did not come, she called again and asked where he was. he told her he had the book in the kitchen. she understood that she had not said where to bring it. he could not see which room she was in, and the words had left that detail open. she asked him to bring it to the front door because she wanted to take it outside. he carried it there, and they went into the garden together. next time, she gave both the book and the place in her request.
why did he choose the kitchen?
it was the place where they usually read together.
what detail had his sister not given?
she had not said to bring the book to the front door.
write the request so it is clear.
please bring the book to the front door. i want to take it outside.
can you know the child chose not to listen to her?
no. he used the place he knew, but the request had not made the new place clear.
make that answer more simple.
we do not know that he chose not to listen. the request had not made the place clear.
finish with them in the garden.
they sat near the tree with the book between them. she began reading, and he asked about the first picture.
give a request with bring about a cup.
please bring a cup to the table.
now say my brother did that yesterday.
my brother brought a cup to the table yesterday.
can i say he brought it as a full sentence?
yes. he brought it is correct for what he did before now.
only give that sentence.
he brought it.
now ask if he did it.
did he bring a cup to the table?
why is the question not did he brought?
did goes with bring in that question. use brought without did when saying he brought a cup.
only give the first request again.
please bring a cup to the table.
i know the word in a sentence, but the sentence still feels hard to understand.
knowing each word does not always give the whole meaning. the order and the way the words work together can change the meaning too.
make that answer shorter.
the order of the words can change the meaning.
can you help if i give the sentence?
yes. we can look at what each part says and how one part changes the meaning of another.
make that reply shorter.
yes. we can look at the parts together.
my example is i do not know whether she left. do i know she left?
no. the sentence leaves open whether she left. it says you do not know the answer.
so know and do not know are important to the whole meaning?
yes. do not changes the sentence from saying you have the information to saying you do not have it.
only give the meaning in simple words.
i am not sure if she left.
write a longer story about two people who remember different parts of a meal. one knows what they ate and one knows who came. do not make one memory take the place of the other.

a brother and sister talked about a meal with their grandmother. he remembered rice and soup, but could not remember which cousin had come. she remembered the cousin who sat near the window, but was not sure about all the food. at first, each thought the other had not kept the important part in mind. then they put the details together. he could tell her what they ate, and she could tell him who had been at the table. neither memory was the whole day. together, the details helped them write a short message to their grandmother, asking whether she remembered the meal too. they left a question open about the day of the visit rather than choosing one without knowing.
what did the brother remember?
he remembered the rice and soup.
what did the sister remember?
she remembered which cousin had sat near the window.
why was putting the details together useful?
each had information the other did not remember clearly.
make that answer a little longer.
putting their details together helped because each remembered a different part of the meal.
finish with the grandmother adding one detail but not every answer.
she answered that she remembered the soup and the cousin, but not the specific day. they kept that question open.
is leaves always more than one leaf?
no. leaves can be about the parts of a tree, or about someone going away. the sentence helps choose the meaning.
make that explanation shorter.
leaves can be about a tree or about going away.
give one sentence for each.
the tree has green leaves. my sister leaves after lunch.
can a word look the same but have a different meaning?
yes. the words around it help you understand which meaning is being used.
make that explanation shorter.
other words help choose the meaning.
now use one leaf.
one leaf is on the table.
what if there are two?
two leaves are on the table.
only give the sentence about my sister again.
my sister leaves after lunch.
give me three short sentences about my plan: i will read, eat, and then go home. do not add anything else.
i will read. i will eat. then i will go home.
why not put eat first?
you gave reading first, eating next, and going home after. the answer keeps that order.
now change the order so food comes before reading.
i will eat. i will read. then i will go home.
can you make that one sentence?
i will eat, read, and then go home.
does that say where i will read?
no. you gave the order, but not the place for reading.
now add the library as the reading place.
i will eat, read at the library, and then go home.
only give the three sentences with that place.
i will eat. i will read at the library. then i will go home.
i have a red cup and a cup that my sister gave me. could those be the same cup?
yes. both details can be true about one cup.
explain why one cup could be enough for that sentence.
one cup can be red and also be the cup your sister gave you.
now i say there are two different cups. one is red and one is blue.
then there are two cups. that new detail makes them different objects.
can you know which one my sister gave me?
no. you have not said whether your sister gave you the red cup or the blue cup.
make that answer shorter.
you have not given the color of the cup from your sister.
she gave me the blue one. how many cups did she give me from this story?
one cup, the blue one.
can you know who gave me the red one?
no. you have not said where the red cup came from.
only give the color of the cup from my sister.
blue.
write a longer story about someone helping with one sentence but asking before changing the whole page.

a child gave her brother a page and asked whether one sentence was clear. he read it, then began writing a different start for the whole story. she asked him to stop for a moment. she wanted to keep the way the story began and only needed to know whether the sentence was clear. he read the line again and asked what she wanted it to say. after hearing her answer, he showed where one word might make the meaning more clear. she chose the change herself. the page still read like her story, and his help stayed with the question she had asked. later, she asked whether he would read the whole page, but that was a new request rather than one she had given at the start.
why did she stop him?
she had asked about one sentence, not for a different start to the whole story.
what did he ask before giving a small change?
he asked what she wanted the sentence to say.
make that answer shorter.
he asked about her meaning before the change.
who chose the change at the end?
she chose it herself.
finish with her asking for the whole page to be read.
when the sentence was ready, she gave him the page and asked whether he would read it from the start.
i need a break from talking. do not say i do not like the person. i am just tired.
i am tired and need a short break from talking. can we stop here for now?
only give the message without an explanation.
i am tired and need a short break from talking. can we stop here for now?
can that still be kind?
yes. it gives your need without saying something wrong about the other person.
now make it shorter.
i am tired. can we stop here for now?
what if i want to talk again later but do not know when?
you can say that the time is open: i would like to talk later, but i do not know when yet.
put that with the short break request.
i am tired. can we stop here for now? i would like to talk later, but i do not know when yet.
only give the sentence about not knowing when.
i would like to talk later, but i do not know when yet.
if the cup is still on the table, did it have to move?
no. still on the table usually says it has stayed there up to now.
what if it is no longer there?
then it was there before, but is not there now.
can i know where it went?
not without more information. no longer on the table does not name the new place.
now i say my sister put it on a shelf.
then the cup is on the shelf, from the new detail you gave.
if i ask whether it is still on the table, what is the answer?
no. you said it was moved to the shelf.
can you know the shelf is in the kitchen?
not unless you give that place too.
only give where the cup is now.
it is on the shelf.
i understood the sentence after reading it again.
that sounds good. reading it again helped the meaning become clear.
use words without become.
reading it again helped you understand the meaning.
can you just say something kind without another task?
it is good that the sentence is clear to you now.
make that reply shorter.
it is good that you understand it now.
now only goodbye.
goodbye.
